newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to announce gun control measures.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to announce gun control measures.

text.p: Spurred by last month's deadly shooting at New York's Empire State Building, President Clinton on Wednesday will unveil a series of gun control measures at a White House ceremony, a spokesman said.

One person was killed and six others wounded on the building's observation deck when Palestinian Ali Abu Kamal opened fire with a semiautomatic handgun he bought last month in Florida. Kamal then killed himself.

Kamal, who came to the United States on Dec. 24, used his motel receipt in Melbourne, Fla., as proof of residency to obtain a Florida identification card. He used the card to buy the weapon at a nearby gunshop.
Kamal was given a criminal background check before he was allowed to buy the gun, but there was no information available about him because he had just come to the United States.

In the Oval Office ceremony, Clinton would announce his support for a bill introduced by Sens. Edward Kennedy of Massachusetts and Richard Durbin of Illinois to prohibit foreign tourists from buying guns in the United States.

He would also announce that Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin would issue a memorandum calling for changes in the form people must complete when they purchase a gun to highlight the existing 90-day restriction on purchases by foreigners.

The president would also announce that the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms was tightening its regulations on how foreign citizens must prove residency before purchasing a gun, the spokesman said.

Additionally, Clinton would announce a measure ordering all law enforcement agencies to require that their personnel place child safety locks on their weapons at home, a safety measure already practiced by ATF and the FBI.
Finally, the president would renew his request for legislation banning so-called "cop-killer," or armour-piercing, bullets.
